These six layers have one default per floor. For each layer, take the column of its floor ([`references/tiers.md`](/reference/architect/tiers/)). Skip a component whose catalog `Tiers` row does not include the floor.

| Layer | Floor T1 | Floor T2 | Floor T3 | Evidence | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ui` | `open-webui` | `open-webui` | `open-webui`, more than one replica | estimate | Open WebUI documents a single-instance default and, for more than one instance, requires PostgreSQL, a Redis-protocol store, an external vector database, shared storage and the same `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` on every replica: https://docs.openwebui.com/getting-started/advanced-topics/scaling. Whether T3 needs more than one replica is not documented and stays `estimate`; for context only, GitLab says that for many customers with fewer than 3,000 users a backup strategy is sufficient and even preferable, and recommends high availability at 3,000 or more users or when downtime would critically impact the workflow (https://docs.gitlab.com/administration/reference_architectures/), Mattermost marks it required at 100 to 2,000 concurrent users (https://docs.mattermost.com/deployment-guide/scale/scale-to-2000-users) and Nextcloud says a component failure interrupts service for up to 100 users (https://portal.nextcloud.com/article/Scalability/Deployment-recommendations/Small-Workgroups-or-Departments) |
| `identity` | None: local accounts in the UI | `keycloak` federated to the existing directory, or the existing OIDC provider | As T2, with department-scoped groups | estimate | Open WebUI documents local accounts with no external identity provider (https://docs.openwebui.com/features/authentication-access/) and Keycloak documents LDAP and Active Directory federation with passwords validated on the directory (https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/blob/26.8.2/docs/documentation/server_admin/topics/user-federation/ldap.adoc), but neither page covers department-scoped groups, and the choice per tier is the spec's |
| `observability` | None: the engine's metrics endpoint where its catalog entry documents one, otherwise its logs | `prometheus` and `grafana` | `prometheus` and `grafana` | estimate | Prometheus documents that its local storage is not clustered or replicated, so the same stack at T3 gives no durable or replicated metric store (https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/storage/); the choice of stack per tier is the spec's |
| `orchestration` | `docker-compose` | `docker-compose`, or `k3s` when `org.kubernetes_experience` is true | The existing Kubernetes or OpenShift, otherwise `rke2` | estimate | Compose's production page calls one server the easiest deployment and points to Swarm to scale (https://github.com/docker/docs/blob/747e4c7528c703b357b1ae83cbbf411229ce59d2/content/manuals/compose/how-tos/production.md), and K3s and RKE2 each document air-gapped image loading and a script install from local files (https://github.com/k3s-io/docs/blob/8b33d6f4106826376a9784bc21d0fbba8dccbc69/docs/installation/airgap.md https://github.com/rancher/rke2-docs/blob/3931bc85192e5d74abdfc43a499b0c6fae2274d2/docs/install/airgap.md); which one a tier needs is the spec's choice, and Docker Engine is outside the catalog |
| `state` | `postgresql`, only when a chosen component lists it under Requires | `postgresql` and `valkey` | `postgresql`, highly available, and `valkey` | estimate | PostgreSQL's failover page documents promoting a log-shipping standby with `pg_ctl promote` or `pg_promote()` but says it provides no software to detect a primary's failure, so automatic failover needs tooling outside the catalog (https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/warm-standby-failover.html); the `valkey` entry has no sourced replication or failover statement, so the row implies no Valkey availability, and the high availability default stays `estimate` |
| `registry` | `distribution-registry` | `harbor`, or the existing registry | `harbor`, or the existing registry | estimate | Harbor documents a minimum of 2 CPU, 4 GB memory and 40 GB disk with Docker Engine and Compose for the installer (https://github.com/goharbor/website/blob/1ce1ac23f8d4969ce587b7ced8afb7954f76115d/docs/install-config/installation-prereqs.md) and, for Helm, externally provided PostgreSQL, Redis, ingress and storage with no offline procedure (https://github.com/goharbor/website/blob/1ce1ac23f8d4969ce587b7ced8afb7954f76115d/docs/install-config/harbor-ha-helm.md); the distribution registry documents TLS, basic authentication and storage drivers and mentions no web portal (https://github.com/distribution/distribution/blob/v3.1.2/docs/content/about/_index.md); where the tiers switch is the spec's choice |

## Writing the decisions

1. Every layer gets a decision, also when nothing is deployed. "None" is a decision with nothing under Components and a rationale, for example "Local accounts in the UI are enough for one team."
2. Infrastructure that already runs goes under Existing, not Components: the directory or OIDC provider from `existing.identity`, the cluster from `existing.kubernetes`, the registry from `existing.registry`.
3. After all decisions are written, read the Requires row of every chosen component's catalog entry. Each required component must be chosen in its own layer or named under Existing.
4. Alternatives considered is never empty. It names the options weighed, in this order: the layer's other cells in the table (another floor's choice, or "None" where the table offers it); the existing infrastructure from the answers; a custom part the user asked for. When none applies, as for `ui`, where `open-webui` is the only UI in the catalog, write "no other `<layer>` option in the catalog" (with the layer's ID) and let the rationale say why the choice needs no comparison.
5. Evidence: the weakest of this row's label and every chosen component's label. A decision with a custom part is `estimate`.
6. With `org.isolation` other than `none`, the catalog documents no separation of departments inside one Open WebUI. Say in the `ui` rationale which separation the design uses (one instance per department, or one instance with groups and one gateway connection per department), label it a custom choice, and list it under verification.
7. A T3 `ui` decision with more than one replica must also add, in the `state` layer, `postgresql` and `valkey`, and the vector database and the shared file storage as custom parts: no catalog entry covers them. Open WebUI's scaling page requires PostgreSQL, a Redis-protocol store, an external vector database, shared file storage and the same `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` on every replica ([`catalog/open-webui.md`](/reference/catalog/open-webui/), caveat on more than one replica). PGVector needs the pgvector extension, which the catalog's `postgresql` entry (the plain `postgres:18.7` image) does not include. Say in the rationale that the same `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` goes on every replica.
8. A T3 `state` decision with `postgresql` "highly available" says what PostgreSQL has built in (streaming replication, hot standby, promotion with `pg_promote()`) and what it does not: failure detection, automatic promotion and fencing of the old primary need tooling outside the catalog ([`catalog/postgresql.md`](/reference/catalog/postgresql/), caveat on high availability). Add that tooling as a custom part. Do not imply that `valkey` is highly available: its entry has no sourced replication or failover statement.
9. A `registry` decision with `harbor` adds Docker Engine and Docker Compose on the registry host: the offline installer needs both, also in a design that runs on `k3s` or `rke2` ([`catalog/harbor.md`](/reference/catalog/harbor/)). Docker Engine is outside the catalog: put it under Existing when the host already has it, otherwise as a custom part. Docker Compose there is the `docker-compose` entry, whose layer is `orchestration`, so it never goes under the `registry` decision's Components. It belongs under the `orchestration` decision's Components: already there when Compose is the orchestration choice, or next to `k3s` when the orchestration floor is T2. When the orchestration floor is T3, the entry's tiers exclude it (the floor of the layer where a component sits decides), so name Compose under the `registry` decision's Existing when it already runs on that host, otherwise as its custom part. Harbor's Helm route has no documented offline procedure, so do not offer it as the offline alternative.

Components used in this file: `open-webui`, `keycloak`, `prometheus`, `grafana`, `docker-compose`, `k3s`, `rke2`, `postgresql`, `valkey`, `harbor`, `distribution-registry`.
